links.reason: Both name Paari, Kapilar and the pool: Akananuru 78 lines 16-24 (கபிலன்... பாரி தீம்பெரும் பைஞ்சுனைப் பூத்த புதுமலர்) and Purananuru 109 line 10 (வான் கண் அற்று... மீன் கண் அற்று, அதன் சுனையே) with the kings who cannot take Parambu (lines 11-13). The shared spring-and-siege image is real and the akam use as settled fame is fair.

Soolamani 1517 only shows the hero holding the hill in one hand (ஒன்றினான் ஒளிவரை உயர ஏந்துபு); no kings or gods hail him and no feat is judged. Tirumanthiram 350 is a crushing and grace; only the mountain-lift is shared, so the note's homage and the 'unpunished lifter' gain are invented.

Kural 1133 is a lover's inventory of lost நாண் and ஆண்மை; the epic verse says that if the love-game cannot be played, restraint by penance is ஆண்மைக்கு அழகு. Only the word ஆண்மை is shared and the two are not claims about the same thing; 'opposite outcomes' and 'path the lover does not consider' are the note's own construction.
links.text_issue: Soolamani flagged sense uncertain; Cintamani 1657 marked uncertain

links.reason: Both are Jain invocations (வென்றான் வினையின் தொகை vs தன்னின் எய்தி... குணத்து ஒள்நிதிச் செல்வன்) but the pairing shows only a shared god praised in different words; 'each praises a different side' is a shared theme, and qualifies does not fit as neither limits the other.

The verse lists withering the five senses and guarding from lying, killing, theft and lust (ஐவகைப் பொறியும் வாட்டி... பொய் கொலை களவு காமம்) and Kural 25 names the strength of one who has quenched the five (ஐந்தவித்தான்). The match is real but illustrative: the verse says nothing of Indra or strength, and the pair adds little beyond a shared virtue.

Naladiyar 23's drums turn from மணப்பறை to பிணப்பறை; Soolamani 936 only describes the din of pipes, drums and horns (துளைபடு குழலிசை துடியொடு சிறுபறை) at the wedding and says nothing of joy turning to loss. The warning is imported from the quatrain, and the verse's sense is flagged uncertain.

Soolamani 901 (Maruci tells the Suramai king) and 943 (he tells the Vidyadhara king that the Suramai lord is coming) are two steps of one errand, not incompatible claims. This is plot sequence mislabelled tension, and 'welcome is mutual' is not stated in either verse.

Both make the woman's eyes the killer: 453 வாட்கணின் அகத்த குறி / கொலைத்தொழில்கொள் and Kural 1083 கூற்றென் பதனை... பேரமர்க் கண்டு. The shared image is real but a common one, and the epic verse is a catalogue of her arts, so the pairing teaches little beyond that.

Civakacintamani 353 has Vijayai put on கல் தோய் நுண் கலிங்கம் with உரவோன் சிறுவன் உயர்க எனவே; 1783 has the same fine ochre cloth (நுண்டுகில் கல்லரத்தம்) listed among what weighs on her (வருத்த) beside the son. The echo is verbal and the contrast between vow and burden is carried by the Tamil.

2502 is a conceit about a pearl necklace lying on the bride's breasts and waist, and Cintamani 27 says Civakan renounced kingship at the Knower's feet. They do not make incompatible claims; 'each wedding adds weight to the later renunciation' is theme and plot forecast, not tension.
links.text_issue: 2502 sense uncertain; grammar of lines 2-3 hard

links.reason: 1135 has Padumukan reason that only the parents could bind him (முலையுடைத் தாயோடு எண்ணித் தந்தை) and 1138 reports the father's stratagem and mother's binding (தந்தை புல்லி... பிணிப்ப). The guess and its confirmation are real, but 'the one force the story allows' overstates one scene, and both verses are flagged uncertain.

1207 shows Tivittan's anger in his body at the envoys' புன்சொல்; Purananuru 72 is Neduncheliyan's vow with named forfeits. Only a taunt and anger are shared; 'lawful in both', 'king's duty', and 'left to stand on others' pledge' are not in either text.

Kural 1134 says love's flood takes the raft of நாண் and ஆண்மை; Kanakamalai says she sold her நாணும் to buy a garland (அரும்பெறல் நாணும் விற்றுப்... மாலை கொண்டேன்). The sale-versus-loss contrast is real, but the gains clause rests on verses 1663 and 1674 that the packet does not show, and the Kural has no manliness in the epic verse.

373 only says the king retires to his chamber with music and tastes அமிர்தம். The link argues from silence ('no word of its pain'), and Naladiyar 60 is about looking at pleasure's pain; the verse offers nothing that the quatrain tests, so the pair is theme only.

1597 has the jester cry that a spirit lives here and eats (பூதமுண்டு அதுபுடைத்து உண்ணும்) and 1600 shows him seeing his own shadow do what he does (தன்னிழல் தான் செய்வ செய்ய). That reading is fair and the later verse answers the earlier, but 'tension' is the wrong type and the verse does not say 'stone'.
links.text_issue: 1597 sense uncertain; 'stone' not in the verse

links.reason: Kural 911 says courtesans' sweet words for wealth bring harm; lines 93-95 have Kovalan clear Madhavi (தன்தீது இலள்) and blame himself (என்தீது). But the letter itself is in lines 87-92, outside this unit, and Kovalan makes no charge to withdraw; one cleared woman is a limit on the rule, not an incompatible claim.

2193 says the kings do not grasp the greatness of ripened tapas (விளைதவப் பெருமை ஓரார்) and fail at the bow; Kural 265 says tapas is practised since it gets what is wanted. The link is real, but 'the one who wins' is not in the verse and the pair mostly illustrates the maxim.

1797 describes the bride walking amid following bees, kings' thoughts and praise-sounds; there is no drum, groom or reversal. Naladiyar 23's warning (மணப்பறை... பிணப்பறை) is imported onto a verse that has no hint of it.

1992 grades gifts as தலை, இடை, கடை by receiver, giver and gift; 2000 says the gifts of one who has grasped the true principles do not fall within the three (முத்திறத்துள்ளும் படாது). The same sage speaks both, so the qualifying is direct, though 2000 is flagged uncertain and 'three' may mean something else.

Kural 320 says all pain falls on those who inflicted pain; Yasodhara Kaviyam 250 says the king and his mother suffered in every birth for killing a flour cock (மாவினால் கோழி... பிறவி தோறும்). The note adds that they 'thought it a rite' and that kin were 'reborn as birds', neither of which is in this verse, so the teaches and gains overreach.

773 is Civakan's vow to see the kings' backs (புறக்கொடை கண்டு) and embrace the lady, and 817 has him see the battlefield (படுகளம் கண்டு) and take her into his house. The vow is fulfilled in its own order; the reading is mild but the Tamil supports it.

1536 gives the mother's hearsay that dying of parting loses both worlds (இம்மையோடு உம்மை இன்றி); 1539 has Kemasari kept alive by the husband's words to the bee. The contrast is real, but 'doctrinal consolation failing' overstates a reported saying, and பேசினார் in 1539 is a guess.

1707 has the king ask the trembling queen and 1708 has him read her vision as a son (அணங்கிவர் சிறுவன் வந்துன் அணிவயிற்றகத்துப் பட்டான்). That is question and answer in plot order, which the graph already records; the teaches is a paraphrase of the sequence.

683 makes her glance a letter (ஓடரி நெடுங்கண் என்னும் ஓலை) sent by her smile, and Kural 1100 says words are useless when eyes agree. But the epic's letter is a one-sided message about her sickness, not the couplet's mutual glance, and the cost to Civakan is not in the verse.

153 has the king take flowers for his queen's adornment (நம் தேவி என்று); 157 has him call Padmavati Vasavadatta. The recurring habit is real and both are the king's, but 'poet's sorrow' is wrong and 'begins the new marriage' is not in 157.

2035 has the pair of the enjoyment land rise to the sky after their span and 2038 says the beasts and birds of that land also rise to the kalpa world (விலங்கொடு உள வாழ்பறவை... கற்பநிலம் ஏறுவன). The later verse extends the former and the land is the common cause (போகநிலத்துள்ளால்).

Both verses use Anni's felling of Thithiyan's punnai at Kurukkai (அன்னி குறுக்கைப் பறந்தலைத் திதியன் தொல்நிலை முழுமுதல் துமியப் பண்ணி... புன்னை), one as a measure of noise and one as a curse. The verbal match is exact and the two uses differ.

62 ranks water, shade and the shared meal as charity (நீர்அறம்... பாத்துண்பானேல்) and Kural 215 likens a wise man's wealth to a full village tank. Both turn on giving water, but the verse does not build on the Kural's figure, and 'makes it literal' is the note's own idea.

757 has Padumukan describe battle as sowing and reaping (அம்பொடு கணையம் வித்தி... விளைத்தபின்) and 820 has the narrator say Civakan put away the battlefield's sin (போர்கெழு களத்துப் பாவம்). The contrast between heroic speech and Jain expiation is real, but the two do not state opposed claims about the same thing; 757's speaker and sense are inferred.

1463 says the discus sent at a blameless man kills the king who sent it (நேமி... மன்னன் தன்னையே செகுத்தது); it does not say the victim's hand turned it back, so the note's agent is not in the text. The return of harm is Kural 319's rule applied, with little added.

1037 has Gunamalai draw a circle in the sand praying that she may embrace Civakan, and 1063 has the wedding drums sound (முரசம் கறங்க முழவு இம்ம... வேட்டான்). The girl's anxious rite is answered by the marriage in the same chapter.

1215 has the god foretell the king giving his daughter to Civakan; patikam 22 says the royals kept him and gave a girl. The link is plausible but the patikam verse is uncertain (கடி பெய்து can mean guard or wedding), and 'all his marriages come as foretold gifts' goes beyond two verses.

749 mocks kings who turn to the sword after failing at the art (வாளினால் மலைந்து கொள்ளின் வாழ்க நுங்கலையும்). Kural 726 is about lacking courage for sword and assembly; the epic kings are not said to be cowards or to fear an assembly, so the pairing rests on the words வாள் and நூல்/கலை.

554 has Kaluzhavegan refuse suitors until the destined time (பாற்படு காலம் வந்தால்) and 848 has him write that what is to come will come (ஆம்பொருள்கள் ஆகும்). The theme recurs, but 848 says nothing of a kingdom, so 'assurance of the kingdom' is not in the verse and the pair is not a development.

Yasodhara 329 says the dharma holds back karma (வினைவலி விலக்குகிற்பது) and leads to சிவகதி; Tirumanthiram 499 is a path of embodiment and knowledge to Siva, obscure and flagged uncertain, and says nothing of a Lord bringing release. The tension is invented, as 'through the Lord' is not in the quatrain.

143 says no one can ward off the ripening of deeds (வினைகளின் விளைவை யாவர் விலக்குநர்), close to Kural 380's fate outrunning any device. But 'trying the mother's device' is not in the verse, whose first half is hard, and the two agree rather than qualify.

272 says every life is like one's own (எவ்வுயிரும் எம்முயிரின் நேர்) and Kural 315 asks what understanding is worth if another's pain is not guarded as one's own. The idea is shared, but the hounds and the hunting pack are not in the verse, and the verse's sense is flagged uncertain.

205 has the king vouch for Kattiyangaran (எனக்கு உயிர் என்னப் பட்டான்) and 260 lists அருள் among what will kill the king. The echo of trust and fall is plausible, but அருள் as his trust is a generous reading of a flagged verse.

737 has the bride drop the garland as if telling the world to do high tapas (உயர்தவமே செய்ம்மின்... என்பாள்போல்), taking Kural 265's motive (வேண்டிய வேண்டியாங்கு எய்தலால் செய்தவம்) and fixing it on a wedding. The verse adds a concrete fruit of tapas to the Kural's general promise.

409 has the astrologer foretell Tivittan will split a lion's mouth within a month (சிங்கம் வாய் பிளந்திடும்), and 828 has a spy report that the lion has been destroyed (அழித்தது... ஒற்றனால் உணர்ந்து). The fulfilment is direct; the new point is the report's route.

1356 urges kings not to flee because fame outlasts the body (பொன்றும் இவ்வுடல் இன்பொருட்டு என்று நிற்கும் இரும்புகழ்) and Kural 780 values a death that makes sustainers weep. The shared theme is heroic death; the weeping-supporters test is not in the verse, so the gains clause is invented.

85 has Yugi free the elephant by smoke and mantra and 86 has the elephant kill the mahouts as it runs. The second is the plot consequence of the first, which the graph already records; the teaches describes the story rather than a link.

67 has the girdle gold lie unclaimed (கொள்ளும் நீரர் இன்மையின்) and Kural 739 calls lands of unsought wealth the real lands (நாடா வளத்தன). The teaches rests on verses 55-59 that are not in the packet, so it cannot be checked, and the pair is mainly an illustration of the Kural.

885 has the maid dispute Civakan's powder verdict and 2043 has her tell the grievance to the disguised Civakan, who condemns the young man (தீயான் மாய்ந்தனன் போலும்). The callback is real, but line 4 is hard and 'wins their trust' is an inference.
